The Helmut Veith Stipend honours the late TU Wien professor by funding outstanding women pursuing a master's in computer science at TU Wien, with emphasis on logic, computation and its applications. The annual deadline is 30 November, making the 2026 round a near-term target.

Programme Highlights

  • EUR 7,000 per year plus a full tuition waiver
  • Dedicated to women entering TU Wien's CS master's programme
  • Fixed annual deadline of 30 November
  • Connected to Vienna's logic-and-computation research community

Who Should Apply

Female applicants to the TU Wien master of computer science with excellent academic records and motivation aligned with logic and computation areas.

Funding and Costs

EUR 7,000 per year towards living costs plus full tuition waiver for the two-year master's programme.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply through the VCLA page by 30 November with the listed documents — admission to the programme is part of the process. Key deadline information: 30 November (annual deadline).

Official Source

  • Official application page (verified link)

About Vienna Center for Logic and Algorithms (VCLA)

The Vienna Center for Logic and Algorithms at TU Wien coordinates the Helmut Veith Stipend, supporting women in computer science within Vienna's logic and algorithms research environment.

Official website: https://www.vcla.at

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 30 November (annual deadline) - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
